skill.name: nature-reviewer
skill.description: Simulates a Nature-style pre-submission reviewer assessment from supplied manuscript material. It returns three bounded reviewer reports and a cross-review synthesis grounded in local Nature reviewer criteria.
skill.summary: Generate bounded Nature-style reviewer reports for pre-submission manuscript critique.

content.value_statement: Researchers often need an objective pre-submission critique before sending a manuscript. This skill turns supplied manuscript material into grounded Nature-style reviewer reports.
actual_capabilities: Generates three reviewer-style reports plus a cross-review synthesis.
Assesses originality, significance, interdisciplinary interest, technical soundness, and readability.
Identifies interested readers and explains why the results may matter.
Flags missing evidence, unsupported claims, and technical failings.
Uses local Nature editorial criteria and user-provided facts only.
Separates reviewer comments from final editorial decision claims.
limitations: Does not decide acceptance, rejection, or official Nature fit.
Does not verify claims against external literature unless evidence is supplied.
Cannot assess missing methods, data, figures, or results not provided.
Is not a substitute for journal editors or qualified domain reviewers.

use_cases.title: Pre-Submission Manuscript Review
use_cases.description: Test whether a draft has clear novelty, significance, technical support, and broad-interest framing before submission.

use_cases.title: Internal Lab Quality Check
use_cases.description: Review a team manuscript with separate emphasis on evidence strength, readership, and unsupported claims.

use_cases.title: Academic Writing Consultation
use_cases.description: Convert a client draft into structured reviewer-style feedback without inventing reviewer identities or editorial outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Abstract
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request using a short manuscript summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this abstract from a Nature-style referee perspective. Return three reviewer reports, a synthesis, and any unsupported claims. Manuscript text: [paste abstract].

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Partial Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this partial manuscript package. Mark what is not assessable, identify technical failings, and explain who may care about the results. Materials: [paste sections].

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test Submission Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for pre-submission risk analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Nature-style pre-submission review. Focus on originality, scientific importance, interdisciplinary readership, technical soundness, and readability. Include the strongest risks first.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reviewer Emphasis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for synthesis across reviewer perspectives
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three reports using the same fact base but different emphasis. Then synthesize consensus strengths, technical risks, and broad-interest concerns.

output_examples.input: A manuscript abstract and figure legends for a new materials discovery claim.
output: Reviewer 1 finds the central claim potentially important but asks for stronger validation controls.
Reviewer 2 questions whether the result is sufficiently unexpected for a broad readership.
The synthesis highlights missing durability data as the main barrier to a stronger case.

output_examples.input: A partial methods and results section without full figures or statistical details.
output: The review marks several conclusions as not assessable from the provided material.
Technical soundness receives lower confidence because key controls and sample sizes are absent.
The broad-interest readout remains tentative until the main figures and comparisons are supplied.

output_examples.input: A full draft where the authors ask whether the narrative supports a Nature-style submission.
output: The reports separate field-local importance from interdisciplinary reach.
They identify which readers may care and why the current framing may be too narrow.
The synthesis lists the highest-priority revisions before submission.

best_practices: Provide the abstract, main claims, key evidence, and known limitations.
Include methods, controls, figures, and statistics when asking for technical critique.
State when materials are partial so the review can mark assessment boundaries.
anti_patterns: Asking for a guaranteed acceptance, rejection, or official editor decision.
Requesting invented reviewer identities, specialties, institutions, or confidential expertise.
Providing only a title and expecting detailed technical critique.

faq.question: Does this skill decide whether Nature will accept my paper?
faq.answer: No. It provides bounded reviewer-style critique and does not claim an official editorial outcome.

faq.question: Can it review only an abstract?
faq.answer: Yes. It will mark the assessment as limited and avoid judging missing methods, data, or figures.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: The default output is three reviewer reports, one cross-review synthesis, and unsupported-claim notes.

faq.question: Does it use external journal policy pages?
faq.answer: No. It relies on the local Nature reviewer source basis and facts supplied by the user.

faq.question: Can it write an author rebuttal?
faq.answer: No. This skill is for reviewer assessment, not point-by-point author responses.

faq.question: What material improves the review quality?
faq.answer: A full draft, figures, methods, controls, statistics, and a clear statement of the claimed contribution.
